summary: Fed hiked on Wednesday. Two days later the 10-year is back at 5%. That's the part worth thinking about: a hike is supposed to cool the long end, and it didn't. Start with inflation. Core YoY fell, but MoM keeps climbing, +0.3% in August. Pretty BAD. It means other factors are pushing inflation, not just the oil disruption. The economy is too hot. Then oil. Attacks continue with Iran, keeping the Strait of Hormuz closed. Simple fix: use our oil reserves to bring prices down, right? We have been, but the disruption is too large. Even better, Saudi Arabia's east-west pipeline had been avoiding this by funneling oil underground and around the strait. Well, it got attacked, and now it's closed as well (the strait carries about 20% of the world's oil, the pipeline another 5%). Now the buyers. Private foreign investors sold $29bn of Treasuries in July, before any of this (TIC data). And on Friday Japan, our largest creditor at $1.2 trillion, hiked to 1.25%, its highest since 1995, with its own 10-year near 3%. Hedge the dollar and a 5% Treasury pays a Japanese fund roughly 2%. A JGB pays 3% with no currency risk. Which means the 10-year at 5% isn't just about the Fed anymore. It's about who's left to buy.
_fedPath_note: Every FOMC decision since the last hike, oldest first: the date, the upper bound of the target range after it, and hike / cut / hold. Drawn as the staircase under the Fed and listed in its card. Add a row after each meeting.

news.what: 10 year is back up to 5%, even after the Fed hike.
Bank of Japan hiked to 1.25%, highest since 1995. Its 10 year sits near 3%.
Stock market is up after the Fed hiked yesterday, affirming control of inflation long term.
The Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75–4.00%. First hike since July 2023.
Mostly political today. But, 10 year is still holding at 5%. Fed decision is tomorrow, will they end the 3-year streak of not hiking rates?
10 year hit 5% for the first time since 2023. The other time it hit that was in 2007...

S&P down as a direct effect of the 12 Sep news, semiconductor index down 5%. Investors questioning growth after Amodei, Altman and Musk said models need to slow down, due to regulation testing and the risks of these models.
